clue.text: Like GBS, brought up to keep a lot of drink in quarters?

indicators.note: one word holding another inside it, as a container keeps its contents

parts.note: someone brought up has been bred, reared

indicators.note: the trimmed drink sits in between the two quarters, so they surround it

parts.note: E (east) is a quarter of the compass; two quarters here are E and E

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter goes

parts.note: whisky is a drink

explanation.surface: A question about George Bernard Shaw, raised to keep plenty of liquor in his lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like lodgings but means two compass points, E and E; 'a lot of' trims the final Y from the spirit, and 'to keep' wraps the result in the upbringing word.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw famously wore a full beard and whiskers, so a person resembling him is whiskered.

clue.text: Agent involved in spying? It makes you sick!

definitions.meaning: a hidden microphone planted for eavesdropping
a germ or virus causing illness

explanation.surface: A spy's tool that also turns out to be a source of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A listening device is a common term for a planted microphone, and an informal word for a germ is the same word.

clue.text: At which place heroin used to be around

indicators.note: the past-tense verb goes round the drug's letter

parts.note: 'were' is the past tense of 'be'
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A question of where heroin was once to be found.
explanation.definitionFit: The interrogative and relative adverb asking for a location means exactly at which place.

clue.text: Way to stop nearly half of 20's hostile attacks

indicators.note: the way plugs the gap, stopping up the shortened word
of a seven-letter word half is three and a half letters, so 'nearly half' keeps the first three

parts.note: refers to the answer at 20 across, INSURER
a road is a way

explanation.surface: A route to halt part of an insurer's aggressive raids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly half of' cuts INSURER to INS; 'to stop' puts ROAD into it, IN-ROAD-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Making inroads means advancing into enemy territory; the plural noun names raids or incursions.

clue.text: Dispatch English composer unknown in Irish town

parts.note: to dispatch is to kill
Thomas Arne, composer of Rule, Britannia!
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: An English composer is killed off somewhere unidentified in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arne was an 18th-century English composer; x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Killarney is a market town in County Kerry, in the south-west of Ireland, known for its lakes.

clue.text: Contact a companion about being on top

indicators.note: in a down entry the 'about' letters sit above the rest

parts.note: RE means about, concerning
CH stands for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: Getting in touch with a friend who is on top of things.
explanation.definitionFit: To contact someone is to get through to them, a synonym of the verb for getting hold of somebody.

clue.text: Carefully place silicon in store

indicators.note: the element's symbol goes in the storehouse word

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse
Si is the chemical symbol for silicon

explanation.surface: Instructions to lay silicon down gently in a warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit something is to set it down or lay it somewhere deliberately.

clue.text: Old crone's coarse tobacco lacking substance at first

indicators.note: the tobacco word goes without one letter

parts.note: shag is a coarse cut tobacco

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of substance

explanation.surface: An old woman smokes cheap rough tobacco with no body to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' drops S, the first letter of 'substance' ('at first'), from SHAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A hag is an ugly old woman, a witch-like crone.

clue.text: English novelist pronounced on poet's boldness

indicators.note: the novelist's surname is spoken, so only its sound counts

parts.note: Thomas Hardy, author of Tess of the d'Urbervilles
Thomas Hood, the English poet; the 's makes his name belong to what follows

explanation.surface: An English novelist pronouncing on a poet's daring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' makes HARDY sound as HARDI; 'on' sets it above HOOD in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardihood is daring or audacity, a slightly old-fashioned word for courage.

clue.text: Woman politician covering northern village where elopers once wed

indicators.note: the name goes round the letter, covering it

parts.note: Greta is a woman's name
a Green is a member of the Green Party

explanation.surface: A female Green politician covering northern issues.
explanation.walkthrough: Gretna Green is just over the Scottish border, where English couples once eloped to marry without parental consent.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish border village was famous for runaway weddings performed by the blacksmith.

clue.text: Irregular rule a girl violated

indicators.note: a broken or violated rule is twisted out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Breaking a rule, a girl has broken out of line.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular soldiers fight outside the regular army, as a guerrilla does.

clue.text: Pulpy food rejected always at university

indicators.note: thrown back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever
up means in residence at university

explanation.surface: Mushy food at college is always sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: A purée is food mashed or blended to a smooth pulp.

clue.text: Composer run into in hospital area

indicators.note: the meeting word sits inside the hospital word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium
to run into someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: A composer bumped into in a hospital zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was the Czech composer of Má vlast and The Bartered Bride.

clue.text: Female child-minder reportedly profits, ignoring one's roguishness

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: only the spoken form of the child-minder counts

parts.note: a nanny minds children

indicators.note: the profits word leaves one letter out

parts.note: gains are profits
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A woman's nanny is said to have profited by mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' makes NANNY sound as NANI; 'ignoring' drops I (one) from GAINS to give GANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shenanigans are mischievous or dishonest antics, the kind of behaviour a rogue gets up to.

clue.text: Governor's girl displaying coarse fabric

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, the title of a governor; 's adds S
Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: The governor's daughter showing off rough cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Hessian is a coarse woven jute or hemp cloth, known in America as burlap.

clue.text: Board engaging medic in Eastern States

indicators.note: to engage is to hold in place, so these letters enclose the medic

parts.note: US is the United States
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A medical board drafting a doctor in the eastern United States.
explanation.definitionFit: To embus is to get on, or board, a bus, chiefly a military term.

clue.text: Support for men only available ultimately behind the scenes

parts.note: to back is to support
a stag party or night is for men only

indicators.note: takes the closing letter of available

explanation.surface: Backing for a men-only event becomes available at last, out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Backstage is the part of a theatre out of the audience's view, hence secretly or out of public view.

clue.text: Knocking back most of the drink, pine throughout dark hours

indicators.note: knocking back a drink sounds like swallowing it, but here it turns the letters backwards
all but the final letter of the word 'the'

parts.note: gin is a drink
to pine is to long

explanation.surface: Downing a drink while yearning, all night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims THE to TH; 'Knocking back' reverses THGIN to give NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightlong means lasting all night, through every hour of darkness.

clue.text: Good to get involved carrying about fruit

indicators.note: the outer letters carry the 'about' word between them

parts.note: to engage is to get involved
RE means about, concerning

explanation.surface: It's good to get involved in carrying fruit about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' slips the 'about' letters in at the join of the two outer pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a kind of plum with green-yellow skin.

clue.text: Model chap, one sent out to produce copy

indicators.note: the numeral is dismissed from the name

parts.note: Archie is a man's name, any chap
I is the Roman numeral one
to type is to produce typed copy

explanation.surface: An ideal man is dispatched to make reproductions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent out' removes I from ARCHIE to give ARCHE.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the original pattern or perfect example of which others are copies.

clue.text: Listener originally lambasting sixties youth over title

parts.note: an ear is what listens

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of lambasting
in a down entry, over means turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: a mod was a member of a 1960s British youth subculture of scooters and sharp suits

explanation.surface: Someone overhears a sixties youth being lambasted over a noble title.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the rank or title of an earl, a noble title.

clue.text: Stratagem old magistrate employed to trap duke

indicators.note: the magistrate holds the duke inside him

parts.note: the Doge was chief magistrate of the old republics of Venice and Genoa

explanation.surface: A trick used by a former official to snare a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a cunning trick or scheme for evading something.

clue.text: Cultivate head of dogwood the first lady cut off

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of dogwood

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A gardening instruction: Eve prunes the top of the dogwood.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop something is to cultivate or build it up over time.

clue.text: One covers crumbling ruins with hesitation

indicators.note: the ruins fall apart, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: er is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly covers up crumbling ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: An underwriter provides cover against loss: the insurance company is the one that covers you.

clue.text: Adhesive substance son squeezed into part of tack

indicators.note: the son's letter is pushed inside

parts.note: a rein is part of a horse's tack (harness)

explanation.surface: A sticky gum where a son pressed into a piece of horse gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Tack is the saddle, bridle and reins of a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky substance exuded by trees, used in glues and varnishes.

clue.text: I enthuse endlessly about tucking into granny's casserole

indicators.note: the inner letters go inside the granny word

parts.note: nan is a granny; the 's makes it the owner of the dish

indicators.note: turned about, so the letters read backwards
the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to rave is to enthuse

explanation.surface: I can't stop raving as I tuck into Granny's stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims the last letter of the enthusing verb; 'about' turns IRAV round to VARI, and 'tucking into' sets that inside the granny word.
explanation.definitionFit: A navarin is a French stew of lamb or mutton with root vegetables.

clue.text: Break top off hand tool making spiked wheel

indicators.note: the first letter of the tool is snapped off

parts.note: a trowel is a gardener's hand tool

explanation.surface: Snapping the end off a tool turns it into a spiky wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowel is the spiked revolving disc at the end of a rider's spur.

clue.text: Conflict interrupting commercial settlement

indicators.note: the conflict breaks into the commercial

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
war is conflict

explanation.surface: Fighting breaks into the advert about a compensation deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a sum granted in settlement of a claim, as by a tribunal or arbitrator.

clue.text: Rascal caught accomplice dipping into booty

indicators.note: the inner letters drop into the loot word

parts.note: swag is stolen goods
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an ally is an accomplice

explanation.surface: A crook is caught as his partner helps himself to the loot.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallywag is a mischievous rogue, a scamp.

clue.text: Atlantic state's supplier of heat and light

parts.note: GA is Georgia, a US state on the Atlantic coast
the possessive 's supplies a final S

explanation.surface: Georgia's provider of heating and lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas is a fuel burned for heating and, formerly, for street and house lamps.

clue.text: Consider senior cleric's responsibility

definitions.meaning: to look at or regard, think about
a bishop's diocese, the area under his authority

explanation.surface: Think about what a bishop is in charge of.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider is to look at; a bishop's diocese is called his see, from Latin sedes, seat.

clue.text: Hotchpotch of salmon pie in port?

indicators.note: a hotchpotch is a jumbled mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A medley of salmon pie served in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hotchpotch of' rearranges SALMON PIE IN. The question mark admits the stretch: the city is an inland river port on the Mississippi.
explanation.definitionFit: Minneapolis in Minnesota stands on the Mississippi and has long served as a river shipping port.
